title: All beings freed, none freed (section 3)
hook: lead all beings to nirvana, yet no being is led, because a bodhisattva has no idea of a self

segments.voice: Yesterday, Subhuti knelt and asked: how should one stand, go on, and hold the mind? Your line: how to hold the mind. What did the asking do when your mind ran off? Day one thousand one hundred twenty.

A volunteer at a food bank goes home after a long shift. Somebody asks, how many people did you help today? It's a fair question. There's a clipboard. There's a number. And yet something about the question sits a little wrong, as if the people who came through the line were points on a scoreboard. The Diamond Sutra's first answer to Subhuti goes right at that discomfort. Free every being, it says. And then: no being has been freed. Today: all beings freed.
screen: `HOW MANY DID YOU HELP?` → `A CLIPBOARD, A NUMBER.` → `FREED, AND NONE FREED.`

segments.voice: First, the size of the vow. The Buddha tells Subhuti how one on the bodhisattva path should think. All beings, of every kind: born from an egg, from a womb, from moisture, or appearing all at once; with form or without; with perception, without it, or neither. All of them, I must lead into nirvana, the kind that leaves nothing behind. Every being, no one left out. It echoes the first of the four great vows from a week ago. Second, the cut. Here's where the diamond comes in. The sutra goes on: and yet, after leading beings beyond measure to nirvana, no being at all has been led. That isn't a riddle tossed off for effect. It's the sutra's first real move. Third, the reason the text gives. Why? Because if a bodhisattva held the idea of a being, they couldn't be called a bodhisattva. Nor if they held the idea of a self, or a living thing, or a person. The helper who keeps a tally of the helped has already turned people into things that can be counted, and turned themselves into the one who counts. The sutra says that's not the path. Fourth, what it isn't saying. It isn't saying don't help. The vow to free all beings stands, at full size. It's saying help without building a self out of the helping. Some readers hear it as freedom for the helper too: no ledger to keep, no score to defend, no hero in the story. And the week behind us points the same way: merit given away, a book honored, two views held in good faith, a wide vehicle looked back on, a morning done fully, a question asked well. Now: no one to count.
screen: `EVERY KIND OF BEING.` · `AND YET, NONE LED.` · `NO IDEA OF A SELF.` · `HELP, WITHOUT A LEDGER.` · then, large: `NO ONE TO COUNT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like: help without keeping score. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one good thing you did for someone recently. Notice if a little voice says, that was good of me. Don't fight it. Just watch it, the way you'd watch a cloud cross a window. Then let the picture change: not me helping them, just help happening, one breath passing to the next. No helper, no helped, no number. If the voice comes back, smile at it and return to the breath. The bell holds the time.
All beings freed. Lead every being to nirvana, the Diamond Sutra says, and yet no being is led, because a bodhisattva holds no idea of a self or a being. Today's word.

Your line: no one to count. Today, do one kind thing and don't tell anyone, including yourself later. Let it go uncounted. Tomorrow, giving without resting on anything. Day one thousand one hundred twenty.

howItsDone: Section 3 of the Diamond Sutra is chanted and studied in Mahayana communities as a teaching on the bodhisattva vow: to free all beings while holding no idea of a self, a being, a living thing or a person.

fork.setup: you've led beings beyond measure to nirvana. what does the Diamond Sutra say has happened?
options: a great store of merit has been earned
no being at all has been led
fork.reveal: no being has been led, because a bodhisattva holds no idea of a being or a self. the help is real; the ledger isn't.

original.note: Sanskrit: the idea of a being, which the Diamond Sutra says a bodhisattva does not hold.

trapdoor: what you thought: 'none freed' means the help doesn't work.
what it means: help every being, but without building a self, or a scoreboard, out of the helping.
what a scholar hears: section 3 names the ideas a bodhisattva drops: of a self, a being, a living thing, a person; they come back in later sections.
